cancelOrder: calls order.cancel() and puts reserved stock back through this.products.updateStock(...). This is a use-case rule carried out through a gateway, not persistence code.

parsedVerdict.reasoning: OrderService is a Service Layer built from transaction scripts. That is a business-layer role in a classic three-layer model (presentation, business, persistence). Its work is coordinating use cases. It checks that customers, products and orders exist and throws a BusinessError if not. It reserves stock through the domain method Product.reserve, cancels orders through Order.cancel, works out discounts through PricingPolicy, and adds up line totals with Money. All of that is business logic. Persistence is reached only through gateway calls (findById, findBySku, updateStock, save). The file contains no query building, SQL, connection handling or storage-format details. Converting between records and domain objects happens in RecordMapping, a separate business-layer file. The file has no transport, HTTP, request parsing, response formatting or framework code. Generating IDs from an in-memory sequence is a small application concern, not a responsibility of another layer. The constructor injects persistence gateways, which raises an import or dependency-direction question. That is checked by other tools and is out of scope here.
